title: Intent-weighted free credits with contextual upgrade prompts and enterprise SQ handoff
creator: Ava Mendes
description:
Overview: Run a two-part experiment to (A) allocate free-tier credits dynamically based on early intent signals and (B) surface contextual, educational upgrade prompts that escalate to an enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) touchpoint for mid-market buyers. Goal is to improve trial-to-paid conversion and surface enterprise sales leads with minimal false positives.

Why now: Current one-size-fits-all credit grants are inefficient: high-activity hobby users and low-intent signups consume the same allowance, while high-potential teams hit limits and churn or contact support. Separately, enterprise conversion is delayed because buyers need SQ answers before procurement. We want to (1) improve credit allocation efficiency, (2) capture enterprise leads earlier, and (3) reduce friction by tying SQ intake into the PLG flow.

Hypothesis: Intention-weighted credits (credits sized by usage signals + company signals) plus contextual upgrade prompts that call out security questionnaire handoff will increase trial-to-paid conversion for mid-market customers by >= 18% and increase enterprise-qualified leads (SQLs) by >= 25% without materially increasing support load (<= +10%).

Signals used for intent weighting: company email domain (company size buckets), initial API/token usage pattern (requests per minute in first 24h), embed/vs-chat usage mix, signup funnel UTM/campaign, and product feature flags used (e.g., dedicated-connector enablement).

Allocation rules (experiment arms):
- Arm A (Control): flat 50k token grant, 30-day window.
- Arm B (Tiered Intent): Small (25k tokens/30d), Standard (50k/30d), Growth (150k/45d) assigned by scoring model.
- Arm C (Dynamic Burst + Decay): initial burst (200k/14d) then rate-limited decay to encourage purchase before expiry; enterprise-eligible domains receive SQ CTA.

Upgrade prompt variants (A/B testing within arms):
- Inline tooltip: contextual cost/limit meter + one-click upgrade CTA.
- Education modal: short benefits + example pricing + link to SQ form.
- Sales pre-fill path: if domain/company size passes threshold, surface "Request security review" and auto-fill basics to start SQ.

SQ integration: create a lightweight initial SQ intake form (12 required fields) that feeds the Enterprise GTM queue and triggers a support SLA. The form will be prefilled when possible and flagged in CRM.

Measurement plan: primary KPIs: trial_to_paid_rate (30d), SQL rate (30d), support_tickets_created_from_trial (30d), average_token_consumption_per_user, cost_per-conversion. Secondary: 7-day retention, net new ARR uplift in first 90 days.

Rollout plan: 2-week internal dogfood -> 6-week public experiment (50% of new signups segmented by cohort) -> analyze -> roll to 100% or iterate.

Success criteria: +18% trial_to_paid OR +25% SQLs with <=10% support increase and positive unit economics (CPA below baseline + 15%).
acceptance_criteria: Scoring model implemented and validated on historical cohort (precision >= 0.65 for top-tier signal)
Backend credit allocation endpoints support three arms and logging for cohort assignment
In-product upgrade prompt variants implemented and toggleable via experiment flags
SQ intake form exists and routes to Enterprise GTM + CRM with prefilling for supported domains
Dashboards show primary KPIs and cohort breakdowns; alerts for support-ticket spikes
Legal & Security approve minimal SQ fields and data retention policy
tasks: Define intent-scoring rules and thresholds (PM + Data)
Implement credit-allocation API and cohort flagging (ENG)
Build upgrade prompt components in Console and SDK (DES + ENG)
Design & implement SQ intake form and CRM routing (PM + RevOps)
Create analytics dashboard and event schema (Data)
Run internal dogfood and gather qualitative feedback (PM + CS)
risks: Over-generous credits increase cost without conversion uplift
SQ friction could scare off PLG users if surfaced too early
False-positive enterprise flags create wasted sales work
Instrumentation gaps could prevent accurate lift measurement
